briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Turns Political as National Rescheduling Nears the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis operators are staring down a possible political lifeline as the 24% wholesale tax becomes a real campaign issue, while brand launches and awards programs keep the state's shelves competitive. Nationally, the DEA's own rescheduling brief argues marijuana no longer belongs in Schedule I, and psilocybin just got a fast lane to market — real momentum for operators willing to look past the near-term noise.

local.text: GOP nominee courts cannabis donors on tax repeal — Michigan Republican gubernatorial nominee John James is promising to repeal or sharply reduce the state's new 24% wholesale marijuana tax, a pledge that has cannabis industry donors opening their wallets for his campaign.

Intrinsic launches as new premium Michigan brand — the relaunched company (formerly Choice Labs and Glorious) is headquartered in Jackson with cultivation in Lake Orion, serving more than three-fourths of the state's provisioning centers.
Best in Grass awards give brands a sales edge — for operators, the real value is simple: awards create trust, and trust helps sell product, with the statewide 2026 competition wrapping this summer.

Industry's tax lawsuits are still alive in court — the cannabis industry has filed two legal challenges arguing the wholesale tax structure amounts to an unconstitutional sales tax exceeding the 6% cap set in the Michigan Constitution, and those cases are pending.

2025 was still a record year for product volume — the sales drop follows a record year, as Michigan cannabis retailers sold more products in 2025 than in any year since the launch of adult-use sales, even as the new tax squeezes margins in 2026.

national.text: DEA's own brief says weed doesn't belong in Schedule I — in its final brief the DEA argued that marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, with a judge's recommendation still pending after the 11-day hearing wrapped in July.

Psilocybin just got fast-tracked toward approval — the FDA granted Compass Pathways' NDA rolling review request and selected COMP360 for the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program for treatment-resistant depression, with executives now eyeing a first-half 2027 launch.

Trulieve makes historic leap to the NYSE — Trulieve Cannabis Corp. received approval to list on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker TRLV, marking a historic shift for U.S. plant-touching operators after restructuring around federal Schedule III reclassification.

M&A wave keeps building after Trump's reschedule order — a cannabis acquisition fund is targeting single-state operators with local brand equity and at least $20 million in revenue, part of a flurry of deals following the executive order directing cannabis to be reclassified as Schedule 3.

States say DEA is moving without much guidance — California's cannabis regulator says the DEA hasn't shown 'any sort of interest' in providing guidance to states about the rescheduling move, a gap operators nationwide are watching as the process drags into late 2026.
